blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PPE donning and doffing safety
stem: Why must healthcare personnel be trained to don and remove personal protective equipment (PPE) correctly?

options.A: Correct donning is needed for intended protection, and careful removal reduces self-contamination or occupational exposure from contaminated PPE surfaces.
options.B: PPE technique can be learned reliably by observation during routine care, so formal instruction is mainly useful for newly licensed personnel.
options.C: Training is primarily needed when a recognized outbreak is underway because routine-care PPE has little potential for self-contamination during removal.
options.D: Experienced staff can omit retraining when PPE products or workplace conditions change because prior clinical use establishes lasting competency.

rationale: A is correct. NIOSH states that donning means putting on and using PPE properly to achieve the intended protection and minimize exposure, while doffing means removing PPE in a way that avoids self-contamination. CDC occupational infection-prevention guidance lists how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE as required training content. B, C, and D incorrectly treat safe PPE use as intuitive, outbreak-limited, or permanently mastered despite changes in equipment or work conditions.
educational_objective: Explain why correct PPE donning, doffing, and training are necessary to achieve intended protection and reduce occupational exposure or self-contamination.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention / National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (CDC/NIOSH); NCSBN
source_document_title: Donning and Doffing PPE: Proper Wearing, Removal, and Disposal; Occupational Infection Prevention and Control: Education and Training; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: NIOSH PPE module last reviewed October 3, 2022 and live-rechecked 2026-08-21; CDC occupational training guidance current and live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: NIOSH Donning and Doffing PPE: donning means proper PPE use to achieve intended protection and minimize exposure; doffing means removal in a way that avoids self-contamination. CDC Occupational Education and Training, Box 4, PPE standard: training includes when/what PPE is necessary and how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear it. CDC Isolation Precautions, PPE section: removal procedures are intended to prevent skin or clothing contamination.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC/NIOSH guidance directly supports correct donning for intended protection, careful doffing to avoid self-contamination, and formal PPE-use training for healthcare personnel.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — appropriate PPE use, infection-prevention practice, and protection of healthcare personnel from occupational exposure.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — relevant official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan safety/infection-prevention page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; PPE-use claims rely on current CDC/NIOSH HTML.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches NIOSH definitions and CDC training requirements.
option_audit.B: Plausible experience-based misconception but safe PPE technique is formal training content rather than merely intuitive learning.
option_audit.C: Plausible outbreak-focused misconception but PPE training applies to routine occupational exposure as well as outbreaks.
option_audit.D: Plausible experience-based exemption but changed equipment or conditions can require renewed training and competency.

cueing_audit.answer_length: All options are comparable in detail, structure, and professional tone; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor depends on simplistic always/never/only wording.
